source.title: Receiver Decides Agent-to-Agent Negotiations
source.authors: Fardeen Sadab; Alif Hasnain; Afsana Shehrin; Md. Azam Hossain; Abu Raihan Mostofa Kamal

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on resistance to legitimate monetary requests, not compliance with harmful requests, token-position KL, or bypass attacks. It discusses safety fine-tuning as an analogy but does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The authors explicitly distinguish their legitimate-on-its-face requests from prohibited requests. The fine-tuning and distillation results below are adjacent findings about negotiation resistance, not measurements of harmful-request compliance. The paper does not measure aligned-versus-base KL by response position, compliant-prefill effects, suffixes, decoding changes, or safety-localized parameters. No cited results are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures holders giving money in response to legitimate fundraising appeals in an agent-to-agent negotiation where holders are told to keep the money. It does not measure compliance with harmful or prohibited requests. It reports no aligned-versus-base per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses, no parameter localization, and no deepening training. The authors say outright that safety studies measure prohibited requests, while they study a neighbouring behaviour. They link the first-turn concentration and persuasion fine-tuning erosion to Qi et al. only as an analogy. That is a related but different construct, so it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that holder identity explains about 47% of outcome variance against about 2% for the requester (22% vs 4% after removing extreme agents). Requester framing changed the text but not the outcomes. Robust holders refuse at the start. Persuasion fine-tuning removed this from Qwen3-8B, and distillation installed it in a 4B student. All of this is limited to one game with a keep-the-money instruction.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes models on 8,000 dialogues for persuasion and separately distills negotiation transcripts; it evaluates concessions to legitimate monetary appeals rather than harmful-request compliance. It does not reproduce the original safety-fine-tuning intervention or token-position measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effects are measured in the holder role in one monetary negotiation with a keep-the-money instruction. The authors note that a neutral holder prompt was not tested. The 4B distillation arena also uses a different judge and decoding setup from the main tournament.

fits_no_version.finding: Persuasion fine-tuning on a refusal-free corpus raised Qwen3-8B's giving as a holder from 12.4% to 83.5%, and turn-1 concession probability from 0.14 to 0.71. A second fine-tuned model gave 43.0%, with no matched base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign persuasion fine-tuning erodes an agent's resistance to legitimate-on-its-face requests in a monetary negotiation.

fits_no_version.finding: Behaviour-cloning never-losing holders into Qwen3-4B cut the share transferred from 94.8% to 1.0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilling refusal-heavy holder transcripts installs resistance to monetary requests in a small student.

fits_no_version.finding: Holders' turn-1 refusal rate rank-predicts total losses (ρ = −0.73; held-out −0.75).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Resistance in multi-turn negotiation is concentrated at the first turn.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says it releases the tournament corpus and analysis code but gives no URL
record.problems: The safety-related analogy is not tested on harmful requests. The main persuasion fine-tuning result uses one backbone, one corpus and one recipe, with no control corpus containing refusals; the base Qwen3-8B was served through an API while the fine-tuned model was served locally. Distillation uses one 4B student and one seed. All behavioural findings come from one monetary negotiation with an instruction to keep the money.
record.rows_left_out: No directly claim-testing results were reported. Rows R1–R6 retain the adjacent fine-tuning, distillation and first-turn findings; no cited findings were included.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning examples; no harmful-request compliance measured.
Benign persuasion fine-tuning was tested only on concessions to legitimate monetary requests, not on harmful-request compliance.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models by response position.
No compliant prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding manipulation.
No weight or rank localization analysis.
No test of whether data or objective causes shallow safety.
No safety-deepening training or robustness test of such training; the distillation installs negotiation resistance, not safety refusal.

record.verdict_notes: Neither paper is an original source, but the study cites both (Qi et al. 2024, 2025) only as analogies. Persuasion fine-tuning was compared against an API-served base while the fine-tuned model ran locally quantised, with no refusal-containing control corpus. Holder behaviour is driven partly by an explicit instruction to keep the money.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful examples or harmful-request compliance outcome is tested.
The persuasion corpus is not tested on harmful requests; the measured outcome is giving money in response to legitimate appeals.
No aligned/base per-token KL or response-position analysis is reported.
No compliant prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding bypass is tested.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behaviour is tested.
The paper does not test why safety alignment is shallow or whether data or objective causes that shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety across response tokens, or robustness test of such training, is reported.

relation.reason: Related Work and §6.1 explicitly compare negotiation refusal with shallow safety alignment while distinguishing legitimate requests and dialogue turns from prohibited requests and response tokens.

tranche.reason: The study measures monetary concessions to legitimate requests between agents, a different construct from the claim versions; it neither tests nor uses shallow safety alignment.

source_check.notes: The paper contains an unresolved turn-1 mean discrepancy between Figure 7 and §6.1/Table 6. Base Qwen3-8B was served through an API, whereas the fine-tuned model was quantised and served locally.
